Some pieces of music don’t feel like just songs anymore… they feel like opportunities to reflect on life. As I’ve got older, I’ve realised time passing isn’t something you notice in the moment. You just feel it suddenly as you start to look back. Good times. Sad times. Mistakes. Missed opportunities. The painful sweetness of nostalgia. Then you wake up (like me) and go “wow, I’m nearly 40. Where did that all go? Can I go back?” 

I hope you enjoy this and it gives you a soundtrack to reflect, as it did for me when I was making it. Thank you for all your support. I adore being able to make these for you.

text:
I turn 62 next February. I'm firmly convinced our minds and bodies don't mesh with comparative time. 
Endless.  
 It doesn't know time, minutes, or hours. Lying in loam, or perched on a branch watching a mouse digging. Living an endless life because “now” is all it knows.  
We obsess over time. Ticking away, rushing forward at times, its regulated gait. I can’t wait! Seconds, minutes, hours, and days, broken into milliseconds; we observe a snapshot of time. Pictures of the past, glimpses of the future, all fantasy outside now’s reality.  
 The curse of time lays bare our expectations. Where do you see yourself in a year? People would say you were crazy if you predicted last year what's happening today. OH, would you look at the time?  
 Obsessive compulsion to regulate and catalog an existence. The fish you caught when you were 9. The day you got married or had your heart attack.  Births and deaths are etched in stone to mark both life and death in some past you remember. While living a life surrounded by those who are still here in this millisecond. 
 But they changed: the Baby and all the childhood memories you remember of her; she is now 34 and has children that she will watch grow into adults. Blessing and curse as you look into the mirror, see the lines and age, and understand that time is far shorter now.  
 That loam-dwelling worm and the owl watching that mouse escape the knowledge of time ticking away. Blissful ignorance that is only triggered by a threat of harm. We know, we all know that time is ticking down. Our brains are hardwired into the ticking clock in milliseconds. 
 Use that time wisely. There isn’t any overtime play for a tiebreaker.

Trent Reznor's reaction to Johnny Cash's cover of "Hurt" was profound. Initially, he found the cover to be gimmicky and weird, but after hearing Cash's version, he was moved to tears and felt a deep sense of loss. Reznor's words reflect the song's power as a medium and art form, as he felt that Cash's interpretation was more sincere and meaningful than his original. This moment underscored the relativity of the human condition through music, as both versions of "Hurt" could not differ more sonically but still resonated with listeners emotionally.

You spend so much of your life looking forward, constantly building toward that next milestone, and then suddenly you're here—in the space where you finally have the perspective to truly see the landscape of your own life.

But even with those heavier pieces, there is a quiet, profound hope. It’s not the frantic ambition of my 30s; it’s a more grounded hope that I still have time to be present, to reconcile with the past, and to lean into the 'now' with a little more grace. text: Good question. It probably sounds a little more fragile as it’s pitched up a tone. On this track I chose to leave the Zimmer piece on the original key - I don’t want to get involved in pitching up entire orchestral stuff! I always try and avoid anything that affects the voice too much. Also - when you split the stems it creates artefacts on the vocal - this is caused by the other instruments crossing into the same frequency spectrum and it creates a kind of warbly jitter. It’s not intentional - just a by product of the process but sometimes it can add something. Similar to the vocal on hurt. Not perfect and slightly damaged.
